extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, patent practitioners, and USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_short: US PTO recordation and secrecy rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules governing recordation (cover sheets, fees, recording date and effect), assignee rights to prosecute and become of record, procedures for complaints about invention promoters, and secrecy/export controls for national-security classified patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of cover sheet errors
rubrics_metrics.description: An error in a cover sheet recorded pursuant to § 3.11 will be corrected only if: (1) The error is apparent when the cover sheet is compared with the recorded document to which it pertains; and (2) A corrected cover sheet is filed for recordation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corrected cover sheet must be accompanied by a copy of the document originally submitted for recording and by the recording fee as set forth in § 3.41.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording fees required
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests to record documents must be accompanied by the appropriate fee. Except as provided in paragraph (b) of § 3.41, a fee is required for each application, patent and registration against which the document is recorded as identified in the cover sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recording fee is set in § 1.21(h) for patents and in § 2.6(b)(6) for trademarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording fee exception for Executive Order 9424 documents
rubrics_metrics.description: No fee is required for each patent application and patent against which a document required by Executive Order 9424 is to be filed if: (1) The document does not affect title and is so identified in the cover sheet; and (2) The document and cover sheet are either faxed or electronically submitted as prescribed by the Director, or mailed to the Office in compliance with § 3.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an exception to the general recording-fee requirement; the cover sheet must identify that the document does not affect title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording date and return/resubmission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of recording is the date the document meeting the requirements for recording set forth in this part is filed in the Office. Documents not complying with identification requirements (§ 3.21) will not be recorded. Documents missing other requirements (e.g., completed cover sheet or required fee) will be returned for correction where a correspondence address is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned papers are stamped with the original date of receipt and accompanied by a letter indicating a specified period within which corrected papers must be resubmitted to retain the original date of filing as the date of recording. The procedures of § 1.8 or § 1.10 may be used for resubmissions to obtain the benefit of USPS deposit date. If not corrected/resubmitted within the specified period, the date of filing of the corrected papers becomes the date of recording. The specified period will not be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of recording is not a validation of document
rubrics_metrics.description: The recording of a document pursuant to § 3.11 is not a determination by the Office of the validity of the document or the effect that document has on the title to an application, a patent, or a registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary, the Office will determine what effect a document has, including whether a party has the authority to take an action in a matter pending before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional assignments treated as absolute for Office purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments made conditional on performance of acts or events (e.g., payment) that are recorded in the Office are regarded as absolute assignments for Office purposes until cancelled with the written consent of all parties or by decree of a court of competent jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not determine whether the conditions have been fulfilled; it treats the recorded conditional assignment as absolute absent cancellation or court order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental Register for governmental interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will maintain a Departmental Register to record governmental interests required to be recorded by Executive Order 9424. The Departmental Register will not be open to public inspection but will be available to duly authorized representatives of the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governmental interests recorded on the Departmental Register will be available for public inspection as provided in § 1.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret Register for governmental interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will maintain a Secret Register to record governmental interests required to be recorded by Executive Order 9424. Any instrument to be recorded will be placed on this Secret Register at the request of the department or agency submitting the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No information will be given concerning any instrument in the Secret Register, and no examination or inspection (or index thereto) will be permitted except on written authority of the head of the submitting department/agency and approval by the Director. Examination must take place in the presence of a designated PTO official. When the submitting department/agency no longer requires secrecy, the instrument must be recorded anew in the Departmental Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic representative designation for non‑U.S. domiciled assignees
rubrics_metrics.description: If the assignee of a patent, patent application, trademark application or trademark registration is not domiciled in the United States, the assignee may designate a domestic representative in a document filed in the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designation should state the name and address of a person residing within the United States on whom process or notice of proceedings affecting the application, patent, or registration or rights thereunder may be served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee may conduct prosecution (post-AIA rule § 3.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: One or more assignees may conduct prosecution of a national patent application as the applicant under § 1.46, or conduct prosecution of a supplemental examination or reexamination proceeding, to the exclusion of the inventor or previous applicant or patent owner (applicable to applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or 363 on or after Sept. 16, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts between purported assignees are handled under § 3.73(c)(3). The assignee(s) who may prosecute are (1) a single assignee of the entire right, title and interest, or (2) partial assignees together or with inventor(s) who together own the entire right, title and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming of record as applicant/assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee becomes of record as the applicant in a national patent application and in a supplemental examination or reexamination proceeding by filing a statement in compliance with § 3.73(c) that is signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the statement in compliance with § 3.73(c) is the mechanism by which assignee status is recorded for purposes of acting as applicant or prosecuting the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee prosecution rights in trademark matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignee of a trademark application or registration may prosecute a trademark application, submit documents to maintain a trademark registration, or file papers against a third party in reliance on the assignee’s trademark application or registration, to the exclusion of the original applicant or previous assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assignee must establish ownership in compliance with § 3.73(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of ownership and requirement to establish assignee ownership (§ 3.73)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original applicant is presumed to be the owner of an application unless there is an assignment. In order to request or take action, an assignee must establish its ownership of the patent or trademark property to the satisfaction of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership may be established by submitting a signed statement identifying the assignee accompanied by either (i) documentary evidence of a chain of title (e.g., copy of executed assignment) or (ii) a statement specifying where documentary evidence of the chain of title is recorded in the assignment records of the Office (e.g., reel and frame number). For patent matters, documentary evidence submissions must be accompanied by a statement affirming that the documentary evidence was or concurrently is being submitted for recordation pursuant to § 3.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial assignee submissions and full-interest accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: If the submission is by an assignee of less than the entire right, title and interest, the Office may refuse to accept the submission as an establishment of ownership unless: (i) each assignee establishes the extent (by percentage) of its ownership interest so as to account for the entire right, title and interest, or (ii) each assignee submits a statement identifying the parties (including inventors) who together own the entire right, title and interest and stating that all the identified parties own the entire right, title and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the Office can account for the entire ownership interest before permitting an assignee of less than the entire interest to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization of signatory for ownership-establishing submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership must show that the person signing is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee by: (1) including a statement that the person signing is authorized; (2) being signed by a person having apparent authority (e.g., an officer); or (3) for patent matters only, being signed by a practitioner of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the required indication of authority is missing, the Office may refuse to accept the submission as establishing ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for establishment of ownership (pre-AIA and patent matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: For patent matters, establishment of ownership by the assignee must be submitted prior to, or at the same time as, the paper requesting or taking action is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an assignee of less than the entire right submits, it must indicate the extent (by percentage) of its ownership interest or the Office may refuse to accept the submission as an establishment of ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue of patent to assignee requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may issue in the name of the assignee consistent with the application’s assignment where a request for such issuance is submitted with payment of the issue fee, provided the assignment has been previously recorded in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignment has not been recorded, the request must state that the document has been filed for recordation as set forth in § 3.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issue-fee assignment statements and correction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for issuance of an application in the name of the assignee submitted after the date of payment of the issue fee, and any request for a patent to be corrected to state the name of the assignee, must state that the assignment was submitted for recordation prior to issuance and must include a request for a certificate of correction under § 1.323 accompanied by the fee in § 1.20(a) and the processing fee in § 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the procedure for correcting the name on an issued patent or late requests to issue in the assignee's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial assignees on issuance of patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more assignee, together with one or more inventor, holds the entire right, title, and interest in the application, the patent may issue in the names of the assignee and the inventor. If multiple assignees hold the entire right, title and interest to the exclusion of all the inventors, the patent may issue in the names of the multiple assignees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The names on issuance reflect the ownership composition at the time of issuance, subject to recording and proper establishment of ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue of trademark registration to assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of registration may be issued to the assignee of the applicant, or in a new name of the applicant, provided that the party files a written request in the trademark application by the time the application is being prepared for issuance of the certificate of registration, and the appropriate document is recorded in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the assignment or name change document has not been recorded, the written request must state that the document has been filed for recordation. The address of the assignee must be made of record in the application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office forum for complaints about invention promoters
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations govern the USPTO's Inventors' Rights Act of 1999 and provide a forum for publication of complaints concerning invention promoters. The Office will not conduct any independent investigation of the invention promoter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Act provides additional civil remedies for persons injured by invention promoters, those remedies must be pursued by the injured party without involvement of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relating to invention promoters and services
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention Promoter means any person or entity who offers to perform or performs invention promotion services for a customer and holds itself out in mass media as providing such services; Customer means any individual who enters into a contract with an invention promoter; Contract for Invention Promotion Services and Invention Promotion Services are defined in the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain entities are excluded (federal/state agencies, qualifying nonprofits, parties evaluating commercial potential/licensing, buyers of business stock/assets, and parties engaged in retail sales/distribution). These definitions determine the scope of the complaint rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint content and form requirements for invention promoter complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must be clearly marked as a complaint under these rules and must include: (1) name and address of the complainant; (2) name and address of the invention promoter; (3) name of the customer; (4) the invention promotion services offered or performed; (5) name of the mass media in which the promoter advertised; (6) explanation of the relationship between the customer and the promoter; and (7) signature of the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The complaint should fairly summarize the promoter's action and include names/addresses of persons associated with the promoter. Complaints and replies must be addressed to Mail Stop 24. Complaints lacking required information will be returned; if complainant's address is not provided the complaint will be destroyed. No originals of documents should be included. A complaint can be withdrawn at any time prior to its publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention promoter reply procedure and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission appears to meet the complaint requirements, the invention promoter will be notified and given 30 days to respond. The promoter's response will be made available to the public along with the complaint. If the promoter fails to reply within 30 days, the complaint will be made available to the public; replies sent after publication will also be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A response must be clearly marked as a response by an invention promoter and must contain: (1) name and address of the invention promoter; (2) a reference to the complaint forwarded or previously published; (3) the name of the individual signing; and (4) the title or authority of the individual signing the response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice by publication when service fails
rubrics_metrics.description: If the copy of the complaint mailed to the invention promoter is returned undelivered, the Office will publish a Notice of Complaint Received in the Official Gazette, the Federal Register, or on the Office's Internet home page. The promoter will be given 30 days from such notice to submit a reply. If no reply is received within 30 days, the complaint alone will become publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an alternate route to publication when service by mail fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints against registered patent attorneys/agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints against registered patent attorneys and agents will not be treated under the invention promoter rules unless the complaint fairly demonstrates that invention promotion services are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons with complaints about registered patent attorneys or agents should contact the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) and the relevant state attorney discipline authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and handling of national-security classified patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications and documents that are national security classified and contain authorized national security markings (e.g., 'Confidential', 'Secret', 'Top Secret') are accepted by the Office. National security classified documents must be either hand-carried to Licensing and Review or mailed to the Office in compliance with the specified routing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant in a national security classified patent application must obtain a secrecy order pursuant to § 5.2(a). If filed without notification, the Office will set a time period within which the application must be declassified, placed under a secrecy order, or the applicant must submit evidence of a good faith effort to obtain a secrecy order to avoid abandonment. The Office may set further time periods if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-publication and withholding of allowance for national-security matters
rubrics_metrics.description: An application will not be published under § 1.211 or allowed under § 1.311 if publication or disclosure would be detrimental to national security. An application under national security review will not be published at least until six months from its filing date or three months from the date referred to a defense agency, whichever is later. A national security classified patent application will not be published or allowed until it is declassified and any secrecy order rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This governs timing of publication and allowance for applications subject to national security concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on availability of certain applications to defense agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications on inventions made outside the United States and on inventions in which a U.S. Government defense agency has a property interest will not be made available to defense agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a restriction on dissemination of certain classes of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy order issuance and compensation direction
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified by the chief officer of a defense agency that publication or disclosure by granting a patent would be detrimental to national security, the Commissioner will issue an order that the invention be kept secret. Any request for compensation under 35 U.S.C. 183 must be made to the department or agency which caused the secrecy order, not to the PTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains who issues secrecy orders and where compensation claims must be directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications disclosing significant part of a secrecy-ordered application
rubrics_metrics.description: An application disclosing any significant part of the subject matter of an application under a secrecy order also falls within the scope of that secrecy order. Any such application pending before the Office must be promptly brought to the attention of Licensing and Review (unless itself under a secrecy order). Any subsequently filed application containing a significant part of the subject matter must be hand-carried to Licensing and Review or mailed in compliance with § 5.1(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents circumvention of secrecy orders by filing related applications; strict routing and notification procedures apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution rules while application under secrecy order
rubrics_metrics.description: Action on the application and prosecution will proceed during the time the application is under secrecy order to the specified points: (a) national applications under secrecy order that come to a final rejection must be appealed or otherwise prosecuted to avoid abandonment; appeals must be completed but will not be set for hearing until secrecy order removed unless ordered otherwise; (b) an interference or derivation will not be instituted involving a national application under secrecy order; (c) when an application is in condition for allowance except for the secrecy order, the applicant and agency will be notified and the application is suspended until secrecy order removed; (d) international applications under secrecy order will not be transmitted to international authorities or the applicant and will be processed only up to the point before transmission would occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must still prosecute to avoid abandonment; however, certain proceedings and public actions are withheld or suspended until secrecy is lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for rescission of secrecy order requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for rescission or removal of a secrecy order may be filed by or on behalf of any principal affected. The petition may be in letter form, must be in duplicate, and must recite any and all facts that purport to render the order ineffectual or futile. When prior publications or patents are alleged, the petition must give complete data as to such publications or patents and should be accompanied by copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets form and evidentiary expectations for petitions seeking removal of secrecy orders.
